//: Which ending plays is decided by 'killed' — the exact set of teachers killed that run. Order and casing don't matter, but each combination must appear exactly once. 'lines' is the phone call (speaker = a teacher id, omit it for narration); 'pages' is the closing narration shown under the title afterwards.

endings.title: PACIFIST ENDING

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Still hard to believe it has been so long since Clover graduated.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I knew they could do it.|Did you hear about what they did recently?

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: No I haven't, actually.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I read on the news that with all the knowledge Clover gained here,|They opened their own succesful indie studio.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: That's amazing! I always knew they had a lot of potential.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Yeah, they really proved themselves. I'm proud of them.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I hope they come back to visit us sometime. It would be great to see them again.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Definitely. We should reach out and invite them for a reunion.|What do you think do?

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I think its pointless. Why should I care for what a student is doing?|Especially now that they finished their studies. They have nothing to do with us.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: You really think Clover isn't thinking about us? About our classes?|Surely, everything they learned was implemented into their work.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I am sure all that we taught them was implemented into their games.|One way or another.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I don't know. I just don't care about them anymore.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Well, I do. I hope they are doing well and that they are happy.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Me too. I hope they are living their best life.

pages: After the events of that day, Clover graduated from Tiltan College and went on to have a successful career in the gaming industry.|They opened their own indie studio and created games that were loved by many.|The teachers at Tiltan College continued to teach and inspire new generations of students, always remembering the impact that Clover had on their lives.|Tiltan would never forget the legacy of Clover and the lessons they learned at Tiltan College.

lines.text: * Ring, Ring...

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Hello, Clover? Are you there?|...I don't think they're here, David.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: It's fine. Just leave a message for them.|They'll pick up the phone at some point.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: It has been a while since you left Tiltan.|I still fondly remember our clash... how you showed me mercy in the end.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I remember that too. I was surprised.|When you first walked into my class, I felt something pure in you.|You really wanted to study, even when the subject was hard.|You never gave up, even when I threw everything at you.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: But it's weird...|Out of every teacher in Tiltan, Yakir was the only one you didn't spare.|Why him?

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: The Tiltan authorities are still looking into it.|I don't have an answer either. No one does.|There was no sign of intent... no clue as to why you'd do it.|We tell ourselves it's because you didn't like him.|It's easier to believe that than to admit there was no reason at all.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Yakir was a good soul.|I had to cover his C# classes for a few years after that.|...I think I liked it a little more than teaching Game Design.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: He was a good teacher. Strict, but fair. Honest.|He was passionate about his subject.|He wanted everyone to get it.|He always saw the good in his students.|Even the reckless ones.|Even you.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Which is what makes it so hard to understand.|Why would you do this, Clover?|We may never know.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: But I know one thing.|And if you ever set foot in this college again

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: You won't come out of it alive.|That's a promise.
* (Click...)
* Ring, Ring....

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Hello? Clover? Are you there?

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: They are probably not going to answer you.|Why would you even call them to begin with? Are you stupid?

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Let me be hopeful.|I want to believe they are still out there, somewhere.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Anyway, we just wanted to call you to say a couple of things.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: First, we want to say that we forgive you.|We know you had your reasons, and we don't hold it against you.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I don't know if I can forgive you.|But I do know that I will never forget you.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Second, we want to say that we hope you are doing well.|We hope you are happy, wherever you are.|I know David could be harsh. Harder on his students than he needed to be.|Maybe something happened between you two. Maybe that doesn't excuse it.|But I don't want to believe you did it for no reason at all.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Yakir, I still don't understand the point of this call.|Are you seriously thinking this person has any shred of goodness?

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I... don't know, honestly.|But when they first walked into my class, they were just a student.|I could tell their intentions were good. They truly wanted to learn.|So why did it end so differently for David?

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Are you really still asking these questions?|Questions. That is all you left us with, Clover.|Questions that may never be answered in this lifetime.|You ruined us. David was a special man.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I am sorry if you feel like I am wasting your time, Dor...|......|But I grew attached to Clover.|We had a real bond. A student and their teacher.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I understand.|But I don't think you should be calling them.|They are not the same person you knew.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I know, Dor...|Maybe you are right about all of this.|But if there is even a small chance they can hear me, then I want to try.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: ...Fine.|Say what you need to say.|I won't stop you.|I am going home. This day has been exhausting enough.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Clover.|I don't know who you are anymore.|But I still remember who you were when you walked into my class.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: That student is someone I was proud of.|And I am still proud of them. Even now.|Even after everything that happened.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I don't think I will call again. I think we both know that.|So take care of yourself, Clover.|Wherever you ended up.
* (Click...)
* Ring, Ring....

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Are they there? Did they pick up?

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: No. Of course not.|I told you this was pointless, Yakir.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Then let it be pointless.|I would rather speak into nothing than say nothing at all.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Clover. It has been a long time since you left Tiltan.|I do not know if you ever think about us.|I hope that you do.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: We buried Dor in the spring.|The college held a service. Most of the faculty came.|His office is still exactly as he left it.|No one has been able to bring themselves to clear it out.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: That chart is still on his wall. The one with the army marching into the snow.|He used to say it was the greatest piece of design ever made.|That it told an entire war with a single line, getting thinner and thinner.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: He never told his students how it ended.|He just let them watch how thin the line got.|He said that was the lesson.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: He was insufferable.|He argued with me about everything. He was rude, he was blunt, and he was almost always right.|I did not like him for most of the years I knew him.|I would give a great deal to argue with him one more time.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: He warned me about you, Clover.|He said you were not the student I remembered.|He said I was being sentimental, and that it was going to get someone hurt.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I defended you. I told him he was being cruel.|I told him there was still something good in you.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: And he was right, Yakir. That is the part you keep walking around.|He was right. You were wrong. And he is the one who is gone.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: ...I know.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I am not going to threaten you, Clover. Dor would have.|He would have promised you something violent, and he would have meant every word.|I am only going to tell you what I have concluded.|I have spent my whole life reading patterns.|I read you wrong.|I will not make that mistake with anyone ever again.|That is what you took from me. Not only him.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: ...You sound like him.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: ...Maybe he was right.|That is what frightens me.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I am finished. I have nothing else to say to them.|Stay as long as you need to, Yakir.
* (A door closes.)

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: ...He does not mean all of that.|He is only tired of being wrong.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Clover, I am not going to tell you that I forgive you.|I do not think that I have the right to.|Dor is the one who would have to say it, and you made certain that he cannot.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: But I am still here. And I am still hoping.|Even now. Even after this.|Dor would call me a fool for that.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: He would probably be right about that too.|...I will keep hoping anyway. Someone has to.
* (Click...)
* Ring, Ring....

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I have one question.|That is the only reason I am calling. Do not mistake it for anything else.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: Why am I alive?

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I have gone over it for months. I cannot make it work.|You killed Yakir, who never raised his voice at a student in his life.|You killed David, who was hard on people because he thought they could take it.|And then you walked past me.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I was rude to you. I was rude to everyone.|I called you names in front of the class. I told you your work was lazy.|If you had come for me first, I would have understood it.|I would have thought, well. That one made sense.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I teach game design. That is my entire profession.|I spend my life explaining why players do what they do.|Give a person a set of choices and they will show you exactly who they are.|That is the whole discipline. That is what I stand in front of a class and say every week.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I have looked at what you did from every angle that I know.|There is no pattern in it. There is no logic in it.|You were given the same options that everyone is given, and you chose this.|In twenty years I have never failed to explain a player's behaviour.|Until you.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I do not think that you spared me.|Sparing someone is a kindness. This was not a kindness.|You emptied this place and you left one person standing in it.|You left me here to look at it.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: The college is short staffed.|I teach C# now. All of Yakir's courses.|I teach mathematics, which I am not qualified to do.|I stand in David's room and I draw hexagons on the board,|because it is the only thing that I can remember him teaching.|The students think that it is a tribute. They laugh.|It is not a tribute. It is all that I have left of him.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: I had something prepared for this part.|A promise. Something violent. I have had the words for months.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: ...I find that I do not have it in me.|A threat means that I believe you are coming back.|And I no longer believe that you want anything from this place.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: My office is on the second floor. You know that. You have been there.|The door is unlocked. It stays unlocked.|If you have an answer for me, I would like to hear it.|If you do not have one, then come and finish what you started, and we can both stop pretending that this was mercy.

lines.speaker: dorbendor
lines.text: ...You are not going to call back. I know that.|People who have reasons call back.
* (Click...)
* Ring, Ring....

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I am not calling to grieve at you.|I am calling because I have worked something out,|and there is no one left for me to say it to.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: You killed Yakir. You killed Dor.|You had exactly the same opportunity with me that you had with them.|You did not take it.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: For a long time I treated that as a question without an answer.|It is not. There is an answer.|I have simply not wanted to write it down.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Yakir and I disagreed for years about how a student should be taught.|He believed that patience revealed a person. I believed that pressure did.|We never resolved it. We were never going to.|He is dead and I am not, and that is not the same thing as being right.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I used to tell my classes that hexagons are the best shape.|That they are the strongest arrangement. That they hold under load.|It was a joke. The students repeated it back to me for years.|It was also, I am now aware, the only thing I ever truly believed about people.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Dor argued with me about everything. Every meeting. Every decision.|He was rude, he was frequently correct, and I did not like him.|There is no one left to check my work.|I did not understand what that was worth until it was gone.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: So. The conclusion.|You spared the one who was hardest on you.|You removed the man who was kind to you, and the man who did not trust you,|and you left the one who pushed you until you broke, and then pushed you further.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: There is only one reason I can construct for that.|You understood me.|Of the three of us, I am the one who made sense to you.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: Do you know what that makes me?|It makes me the part of this school that you agreed with.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I have not raised my voice at a student since it happened.|I do not push anyone anymore. I cannot make myself do it.|I stand in front of a class and I am gentle with them,|and I have no idea whether I am helping them or abandoning them.|Three years of certainty, gone in a single afternoon.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: I want to be clear about one thing.|If you left me alive because you believed that I would understand you,|then you made an error.|I do not understand you. I have no wish to.|Whatever you saw in me, it was not agreement.

lines.speaker: david
lines.text: ...I would like to tell you that you were wrong about me.|I find that I cannot say it with any confidence.|And I have never in my life said a thing that I could not prove.
* (Click...)
* Ring, Ring....

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Hello, Clover.|...I do not know if this is still your number.|It is the one written on your student form. It is all that I have.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I have started this call four times this week.|Every time, I hung up before it rang.|I am not going to do that again.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I have been going through my old files.|Every assignment that you ever submitted to me is still on my computer.|I keep all of my students' work. I have always done that.|I have read yours again. All of it. More than once.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I was looking for something. A sign. Anything at all.|A comment in the code. A variable name. Something ugly hiding in there.|Something that would have told me what was coming.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: There is nothing.|It is just code, Clover. It is good code.|Your loops were clean. You commented properly, which almost nobody does.|You fixed the bug in your final project by yourself, and you were proud of it.|I remember that you were proud of it.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: So I am left with the other possibility.|That there was never anything in you to find.|That whatever happened, happened afterwards.|And that I was standing right there when it did, and I did not see it.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I have thought about it every single day.|What I should have asked you. What I should have noticed.|You sat in my classroom for a year, and I believed that I knew you.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Dor never trusted anyone. Not the students, not the staff, not me.|He used to tell me that I was soft. That people would take advantage of it.|He called me a fool more times than I can count.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: There is no one left to call me that.|I did not expect to miss it.|I would like very much to be called a fool again.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: David and I argued about how hard a teacher should push.|He believed that pressure revealed people. I believed that patience did.|We never settled it. We were never going to settle it.|His board is still covered in hexagons. Nobody has erased it.|I do not think that anybody is going to.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: Here is the part that I do not know how to say properly.|I still believe that there is something good in you.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I know how that sounds. I know exactly what you did.|I know that a reasonable man would have stopped believing it by now.|Dor would tell me that this is the problem. That this is precisely what killed him.|And I cannot prove that he was wrong.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: But I have never once looked at a student and seen nothing.|Not once, in all the years that I have done this.|I am not going to learn how with you.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: So I am going to tell you where I am.|I teach in the same room. The one with the blind that never closes properly.|I arrive early. I have always arrived early.|If you come, I will be there.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I am not asking you to explain yourself.|I am not asking you to apologise. I do not think it would help either of us.|I would simply like to talk to you.|That is all. That is the entire reason for this call.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I know what I am offering you. I am not confused about it.|I should be afraid of you.|I am not.

lines.speaker: yakir
lines.text: I am still your teacher, Clover.|That does not stop because of what you did.
* (Click...)

endings.title: GENOCIDE ENDING

lines.text: * Ring, Ring....
* Ring, Ring....
* There is no one left to answer.

pages: After the events of that day, Tiltan College was closed indefinitely. You were captured and overwhelmed by the police force in the area.|You were sentenced to life in prison for the murders of Yakir, David, and Dor Ben Dor.|The college was left in ruins, and the students who survived were left to pick up the pieces of their shattered lives.|The world would never forget the tragedy that unfolded at Tiltan College, and you would forever be remembered as the one responsible for it.
